entries.title: Two lanterns at Old North Church

tiers.kids: On the night of April 18, 1775, two lanterns were hung in the tower of Old North Church in Boston as a warning signal.
tiers.everyday: On the evening of April 18, 1775, two lanterns hung in Old North Church's bell tower warned that British troops were crossing the Charles River toward Lexington and Concord.
tiers.student: On the evening of April 18, 1775, Robert Newman and John Pulling climbed Old North's bell tower and briefly hung two lanterns, a signal from the tallest structure in Boston that British troops were crossing the Charles River and heading toward Lexington and Concord (NPS). entries.title: NSFNET and the public internet

tiers.kids: In the late 1980s and 1990s, a science network grew into the internet that everyone can use.
tiers.everyday: NSF launched NSFNET in 1986. It grew from about 2,000 computers to more than 2 million by 1993, and NSF shut it down in 1995 as commercial internet service took over.
tiers.student: NSF launched NSFNET in 1986 to link researchers to supercomputer centers; it became the de facto U.S. internet backbone, growing from about 2,000 computers to more than 2 million by 1993. entries.title: America 250

tiers.kids: On July 4, 2026, the United States turned 250 years old.
tiers.everyday: July 4, 2026 marked 250 years since Congress approved the Declaration of Independence in Independence Hall, Philadelphia. The celebration there included a July 4 ceremony on Independence Mall, close to the Liberty Bell.
tiers.student: July 4, 2026 marked 250 years since the Second Continental Congress approved the Declaration of Independence in Independence Hall. The anniversary centred on Independence Hall in Philadelphia: the National Park Service closed the hall from November 13, 2025 to January 28, 2026 for preservation work to prepare it for the 250th, and on the morning of July 4, 2026 a free Celebration of Freedom Ceremony was held on Independence Mall in Independence National Historical Park. The original Liberty Bell is displayed in the same park, in the Liberty Bell Center near the hall.
